name: Decimal Mod Multiplication
description: A deterministic 5-tape decimal Turing machine computing (a*b) mod p. The user enters ordinary base-10 integers directly on tapes 1, 2, and 3; tapes 4 and 5 start empty. The TM itself adds boundary markers, repeatedly decrements b, adds a to the running result, reduces the result by repeated decimal subtraction of p, removes its private markers, and halts with the ordinary base-10 remainder on tape 5. No decimal-to-binary conversion or external arithmetic orchestration is required. This is a simple correctness/compiler-reference machine rather than an asymptotically efficient modular multiplication algorithm.

input_convention.tape_0_A: Enter a as ordinary decimal digits, e.g. 123. No sign and no leading zeros except the number 0.
input_convention.tape_1_B: Enter b as ordinary decimal digits, e.g. 456. No sign and no leading zeros except the number 0.
input_convention.tape_2_P: Enter p as an ordinary positive decimal integer >= 2, e.g. 7. Prime p is fine but primality is not required by the machine.
input_convention.tape_3_WORK: Leave empty. This reference implementation keeps the fourth tape unused/reserved.
input_convention.tape_4_RESULT: Leave empty. On HALT this tape contains the decimal value (a*b) mod p with no private markers.
input_convention.heads: All five heads start at cell 0.
input_convention.private_symbols: The TM internally writes ^ as a left boundary and # as a right boundary. It removes these from the result tape before HALT.

algorithm.summary: Repeated-addition modular multiplication in decimal notation.
steps: Add private ^ and # boundary markers to the three decimal inputs and initialize the result to 0.
Scan b. If b is zero, clean the result tape and halt.
Decrement b by one using ordinary decimal borrow.
Add a to the running result using ordinary decimal carry.
Compare the running result with p by decimal length and then lexicographically.
While result >= p, subtract p using ordinary decimal borrow and normalize leading zeros.
Erase the result tape's private markers and halt with an ordinary decimal remainder.
algorithm.performance_note: The algorithm is intentionally simple. Its running time can be very large for large b or for a much larger than p, because it uses repeated addition and repeated subtraction. It is intended as a transparent general-TM compiler and runtime test.

verification.verification_scope: Random a in [0,80], b in [0,50], p in [2,29], plus named examples.
